messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: gpu-serving-prod - elevated 429s and sustained queue growth (>60). Autoscaler reported failed handshake with pool-manager; 'scale_request_timeout' seen in logs. Paging sre-oncall.

Maya S.: I see spike in requests to /v1/generate from a small set of keys, 99th pct latency jumped. Queue length on hotpath = 68. GPUs at 98% util, but autoscaler shows no new nodes requested (scale_attempts=0). :rotating_light:

Ryan C.: looking. Checking autoscaler logs now. Can someone grab recent tokenbucket/tier configs? Suspect a tier policy pushed yesterday might be denying burst units.

sre-oncall: grabbing configs -> `rdctl get config ratepolicy prod-hotpath --format json`

Infra-Leo: quoting relevant fields from prod config:
```
"tiers": [
  {"name": "prod", "units": 1000},
  {"name": "hot-burst", "units": 0, "burst_enabled": false}
]
"autoscaler": {"scale_limit": 4, "handshake_timeout_ms": 12000}
```
Looks like hot-burst units got set to 0 during the rollout last night.

Maya S.: Oof. That explains tokenbucket rejections causing 429s and autoscaler not stepping because routing kicked to lower tiers and ratepolicy returned 429 early. But GPUs still saturated from existing sessions so autoscaler should've requested more nodes — scale_limit=4 might be blocking further scale.

Ryan C.: Confirming autoscaler logs: `ERROR pool-manager handshake: max_scale_reached` and earlier `WARN scale_attempt_failed: handshake_timeout`. The scaler attempted to open new gpu nodes but handshake didn't complete before timeout. Handshake_time median = 15000ms > configured 12000ms. Earlier infra networking change increased setup latency.

Jenks: Oncall mitigation plan: 1) Re-enable hot-burst units temporarily 2) Increase autoscaler handshake_timeout and scale_limit 3) Throttle aggressive API keys to reduce new queue ingress 4) Failover some traffic to smaller model variant to reduce per-request GPU time.

sre-oncall: Agreed. I'll apply step 1 and 2. Applying tokenbucket patch: `rdctl patch ratepolicy prod-hotpath --set tiers.hot-burst.units=500 --apply`

Infra-Leo: Increasing autoscaler limits now: `rdctl patch autoscaler gpu-pool --set handshake_timeout_ms=30000 --set scale_limit=8`

Maya S.: Rolling the smaller model fallback: `routing set-weight /v1/generate model=redwood-sm:0.2` (20% traffic to smaller model) — doing a staged rollout.

CS-Alex: Notifying impacted customers: Several customers on medium plans seeing 429s for ~4-6 minutes. I'm sending the initial blast and will update once we stabilize.

sre-oncall: Patch applied. Re-checking metrics: queue_len falling from 68 -> 42 in 60s. 429 rate down 80%. GPUs still high but new allocation event in progress (scale request queued).

Ryan C.: Confirm handshake ms dropped since timeout increase? Looking at new logs: handshake attempts now succeed ~18s. Good. scale events: +2 nodes requested, expected ready in ~90s.

Maya S.: While we wait for new nodes, continuing to throttle noisy keys. Ran this command to set per-key limit: `rdctl rate-limit update --key noisy-client-123 --limit 2rps --burst 5`

Jenks: Also toggled KV-prefetch cache to reduce duplicate token construction on hot requests: `feature toggle cache-prefetch=true --service=runtime` Reduced  p99 token generation CPU work ~30%.

Infra-Leo: New nodes landing. pool-manager reports nodes_added=2, pool_size now 6 (was 4). GPU util trending down to 75%.

sre-oncall: Queue len now stabilized at 12. 429s down to baseline. Re-enabling hot-burst to original planned values after autoscaler catch-up? Recommend keep hot-burst=500 for 15m to ensure smoothing, then revert.

Maya S.: Agreed. I'll keep the smaller model weighting until p50 latency stabilizes under 400ms for 5m.

CS-Alex: Customer update: "We saw transient 429s for ~9 minutes, engineering applied mitigation and service is healthy. We'll follow up with postmortem." Customers acknowledged.

Ryan C.: Root causes we should track: 1) ratepolicy change set hot-burst units to 0 during last config rollout 2) autoscaler handshake_timeout and scale_limit were too restrictive given recent node provisioning latency increase 3) excessive burst from a small set of clients (noisy keys) amplified queue growth.

Jenks: Quick runbook notes added to incident doc: - Revert risky ratepolicy rollouts behind feature flag - Autoscaler: increase handshake_timeout_ms default to 30s and add slow-provision detection to avoid max_scale_reached false positives - Add alert for tokenbucket.units==0 on prod hot tiers - Add per-key anomaly detection to throttle noisy clients automatically.

sre-oncall: Creating postmortem ticket and assigning owners: ratepolicy config rollback -> Maya S.; autoscaler tuning & infra investigation -> Infra-Leo; noisy client detection -> Ryan C.; customer comms -> CS-Alex.

Maya S.: Final checks: all metrics show stable for 10m, closing pager in 5m if no regressions. Leaving runbook entry + links to logs: `https://logs.prod/gpu-serving/1729554321`

CS-Alex: Thanks team. I'll follow up with affected customers and include expected remediation timeline for full config audit. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: gpu-serving-prod - 429 spike mitigated and autoscaler recovered. Incident channel will be archived to postmortem when ticket created.
